root: ^Sunak: Approach the road ahead with caution, traveler.
^ This sand feels foreign, even to those long acquainted with the land of Slepbone.
^What can you tell me about Sunkenland?

c-0: ^Sunak: I am Sunak. Unlike my father and his father before him, I was born free — yet never unbound.
^ Their chains may have rusted away, but the memory of bondage still clings to our blood.
^ We, the Sundered, carry the weight of our ancestors’ pain, not as shame, but as remembrance.
c-1: ^Sunak: Once, this place shimmered with golden leaves and dwarven song.
^ The halls of Obsidian Keep echoed with laughter — until the curse took root.
^ King Thrommond’s wrath fell upon his own blood when a Sundered dared to love his daughter.
^ The keep withered, its heart turned to stone, and its king to legend.
^ Now, Sunkenland breathes only through memory. We remain, for no other soil would bear our name.
^ The past binds us here, as surely as any chain once did.

s0: ^Sunak: The Hawk Band is recruiting again. Beware — they test with blood before they trust with word.
s1: ^Sunak: They say Danuris, the dragon, still rots in the keep’s depths. His cries shake the stones when the moon wanes.
s2: ^Sunak: The stench you smell belongs to Gorth, the Gatekeeper. He hungers for company — and seldom lets it leave.
